summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, morbid obesity, type 2 diabetes, and chronic venous thromboembolism was admitted for dyspnea on exertion and significant weight gain. She was found to have pulmonary edema due to volume overload, a subtherapeutic INR from discontinued warfarin, and a urinary tract infection with E. coli and Enterococcus. She was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral furosemide, and bridged with heparin before resuming warfarin. A CT scan revealed findings suggestive of sarcoidosis, prompting a pulmonary referral. She developed transient hyperkalemia, likely due to heparin-induced hyperaldosteronism, and experienced lightheadedness from volume shifts, managed with physical therapy. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to extended care with follow-up plans for sarcoidosis, iron deficiency anemia, and anticoagulation management.
